As of 305 PM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...A Tornado Watch has been issued for portions of
south-central and SE VA as well as NE NC through 8 PM.

Afternoon surface analysis depicted the occluded center of the 
remnants of Isaias across the southern Appalachians with a 
secondary surface low near the VA/NC border between Danville and
Greensboro. This secondary low will continue to track NE this
afternoon, pushing the CAD warm front north. Mesoanalysis
depicted 500 J/kg of MLCAPE along the edge of the warm front
pushing into portions of south-central VA, SE VA, and NE NC.
Mesoanalysis suggests the instability continues to push north
through the afternoon with 500 J/kg of MLCAPE potentially
pushing all the way into the Northern Neck and Eastern Shore by
this evening. Additionally, 1000 J/kg of MLCAPE could push into
SE VA/NE NC later this afternoon. This is colocated with
effective SRH around 200 m2/s2 along and ahead of a broken line
of supercells currently located across north-central NC. As
such, the tornado threat will continue to increase this
afternoon across south-central VA, SE VA, and NE NC with sig tor
values increasing to around 1. As such (and per collaboration
with neighboring offices and SPC) a Tornado Watch has been 
issued from Mecklenburg NE through Charles City County and east
through the Hampton Roads region. This also includes all 
counties/cities south of that line including NE NC. The Tornado 
Watch is in effect until 8 PM this evening. Will note that an 
expansion of the watch is possible later this afternoon if the 
threat appears to continue beyond the footprint of the current 
watch. However, some uncertainties regarding the degree of 
destabilization remain given stratiform precip ahead of the 
broken line of storms. The severe threat should wane this 
evening as the system begins to move out of the area and we 
loose diurnal instability. Will also note that a low-end risk 
for severe storms exists for the remainder of the FA outside of 
the Tornado Watch. The greatest uncertainty is across portions 
of central VA as some CAMs show the line of supercells arching 
across this region and potentially redeveloping later this 
afternoon into this evening along the triple point of the 
surface low. However, CAD has held on with temps in the 60s in 
Nottoway and Prince Edward Counties north. Therefore, will need 
to watch this area as well for any potential redevelopment later
today if destabilization can occur (a conditional threat).

Outside of the tornado threat, these storms will likely produce
very heavy rainfall rates. Therefore, locally heavy rain and
flash flooding is possible, especially if convection can
somewhat stall along the triple point. Convection tapers off
this evening from SW to NE behind the line of storms. However,
the low associated with the remnants of Isaias to the west of 
the surface low does look to move through the area overnight. 
CAMs show additional showers with this low tonight into early 
Mon morning across mainly the northern half of the area.


KEY MESSAGE 2...A brief warmup is expected early next week with 
cooler temperatures later in the week. Much cooler temperatures
arrive next weekend.

An upper level ridge centered across the central CONUS 
gradually builds into the region through the week. Meanwhile, 
surface high pressure remains centered across the Deep South 
through midweek before a second area of high pressure builds in 
from the north late in the week. This will bring a warmup with 
highs in the 70s for most Mon, lower 80s for most Tue (upper 
70s across the Eastern Shore), and mid-upper 80s (most in the
upper 80s) Wed. Some locations could approach 90F on Wed across
portions of central/SE VA and NE NC. Slightly cooler
temperatures return from Thu to Fri behind a cold front with 
highs in the low- mid 70s north to lower 80s south. However,
these temperatures are still above normal for most (apart from
northern portions of the FA). Actually cooler weather returns
next weekend as a strong cold front moves into the region with a
strong area of high pressure building in behind it. Breezy NW
winds and highs in the mid-upper 50s NW to mid 60s SE are
expected next weekend underneath a strong trough. If this trough
is fully realized, we could be looking at the first frost of the
season across portions of the area. The latest NBM has lows in
the mid-upper 30s across the Piedmont and mid-upper 40s closer
to the coast Sat and Sun nights. Otherwise, dry weather
continues for most of the week apart from the chance for some
scattered showers Thu night into Fri across mainly N/NE 
portions of the FA.


KEY MESSAGE 3...Coastal Flood Advisories and Statements continue through 
late afternoon/early evening for portions of east-central VA 
along the Bay, tidal Rappahannock/Potomac, and across the bayside
of the lower Maryland and VA eastern shore for nuisance to Minor
flooding.
